decisions.reason: The cutting and creasing finisher sits close to the core distributed portfolio and costs little to keep, and two years without a clear negative signal do not yet justify abandoning the option.

As a low-cost complementary module that builds on established systems, it keeps future workflow-integration options open at minimal holding cost, though limited visibility slightly raises the risk of withdrawal.
The B2 multifinisher is a flagship aligned with the firm's automation direction, and its prospects justify continued commitment rather than abandonment.
A documented inline customer installation has partly resolved the uncertainty in its favor, and keeping this add-on costs little.
